title: Jupyter real kernel rootfs identity

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: A Jupyter benchmark must prove the actual kernel process that executed a request, not only the Emacs process or `jupyter' CLI.
hypothesis: A temporary Python kernel launched through `jupyter_client' should execute one request, return a matching shell reply and IOPub idle state, and print rootfs identity from inside the kernel.
minimal_fixture: A temporary `jupyter_client.KernelManager' Python kernel launched from the selected rootfs.
predicted_behavior: Production mode should execute code in a real kernel with matching request ids, rootfs-owned Python executable, stable Insula run id, and idle completion evidence.

independent_checks.name: real Jupyter kernel probe ran in production
kernel request reached ok reply and idle
kernel sees stable Insula run id
kernel executable and cwd are rootfs/runtime owned

counterexample: A checker that accepts the right printed value can miss execution on the wrong kernel, duplicate retries, or an unknown request outcome.
derived_gym_requirement: Jupyter actions must track kernel incarnation, request id, shell reply, parent-header outputs, idle/completion state, and kernel-side rootfs identity.
